messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: service=frontend/inference-gateway p99 latency > 5s and gateway 502/504s spike detected since deploy deploy-2026-03-15-1402 (canary started 14:02 UTC). Affected region: us-west-2. Link: https://grafana.redwood/g/dash/inference-gateway

matthew: oncall here – acknowledged. Paging @oncall-sre and @sara. Any initial observations? :rotating_light:

sara: I’m on it. Looking at canary logs now. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~6.8s. 502s correlate with upstream timeouts to model-backend (connection timeout).

raj: If it’s upstream timeouts we should consider immediate rollback of the canary. What’s the canary traffic percentage?

sara: Canary at 10% right now. Quick log snippet from gateway:

```
[2026-03-15T14:05:12Z] ERROR upstream request failed: dial tcp 10.32.45.12:8080: i/o timeout
[2026-03-15T14:05:13Z] WARN connection pool exhausted: active=500 max=500
[2026-03-15T14:05:14Z] ERROR 502 response returned to client, route=/v1/generate
```

matthew: customer-impact check: per-tenant dashboards show ~1.8% 5xx across the region, top 10 tenants account for ~60% of the error volume. Customer Success flagged a few real-time complaints. @customer-success can you paste any customer reports?

customer-success: Received a handful of complaints from two enterprise customers reporting timeouts for chat and API failures since ~14:03 UTC. They saw retries from their side. Flagged as Sev-2 so far.

sara: Running quick curl against health endpoints for model-backend: `curl -s -D - http://10.32.45.12:8080/health` returns no response before timeout. Also seeing a sudden increase in ephemeral connection counts on the host. Hypothesis: new runtime change in deploy adjusted upstream keepalive or connection pool sizing which exhausted sockets under bursty traffic.

raj: Which commit in the deploy? Any obvious config diffs?

sara: Deploy metadata: commit a7f3b4e -> feature: multiplexing: adjust upstream.conn_max from 1000 -> 500 and keepalive timeout decreased. Diff: `upstream.conn_max: 1000 -> 500` `upstream.keepalive: 90s -> 30s`

oncall-sre: @matthew if we can rollback the canary to stop new errors that seems safest. We should also add a temporary circuit breaker so model-backend is not hammered while we investigate.

matthew: Agreed. @deploy-bot initiate rollback of deploy-2026-03-15-1402 for inference-gateway canary. Command: `/deploy rollback inference-gateway deploy-2026-03-15-1402 --scope=canary`

deploy-bot: Command received: starting rollback of inference-gateway deploy-2026-03-15-1402 (canary scope).

deploy-bot: Rollback in progress... reverting traffic allocation -> previous version, monitoring canary health.

sara: While rollback is running I pushed a temp nginx circuit-break config to limit concurrent upstream requests per worker to 200 and added 5s proxy_read_timeout as stop-gap.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Canary traffic reverted to previous stable version. New canary traffic at 0%. Health checks passing on stable.

matthew: Nice. Post-rollback telemetry: p99 back down to ~140ms after ~90s, 5xx rate trending down toward baseline. Customer error volume decreasing.

raj: Good. Next actionable items: 1) revert the config change in mainline (conn_max/keepalive) 2) create a targeted fix to add proper connection pooling controls and backpressure 3) add a deploy guard that runs a quick upstream connection stress test during canary before increasing traffic.

sara: I’ll open the PR to revert commit a7f3b4e and add the connection pool tuning with safe defaults. I’ll also add a unit that validates conn_max >= expected_conn_count before deploy.

customer-success: Notifying the two impacted customers with the rollback update and ETA for root cause. They asked for an incident summary.

eve: Assigning postmortem to @sara and @raj. Please include timeline, root cause (config change), why the canary didn't catch it, and remediation steps (revert, deploy guard, circuit-breakers). Tag the incident Sev-2 and set RFC for next week.

matthew: Handoff to oncall for monitoring. Keep channel open for 30 minutes of watch. If errors reappear escalate immediately. Thanks everyone for quick action. :thumbsup:

sara: I’ll follow up with the PR link and brief writeup in #postmortems. Will include exact metrics and the log snippets. Closing this thread when we hit 30m clean window.
